stem: Connected Bulbs: Bulb A ($1.00\text{~L}$, containing $\text{Ne}$ at $2.0\text{~atm}$) and Bulb B ($2.00\text{~L}$, containing $\text{Ar}$ at $1.0\text{~atm}$) are connected by a closed valve at constant temperature. When the valve is opened, what is the final partial pressure of neon?
Gas Kinetics: If the absolute temperature of an ideal gas is doubled while its volume is halved, what happens to the pressure of the gas?
Stoichiometry & Combustion: What volume of oxygen gas at STP is required to completely combust $5.60\text{~g}$ of butane ($\text{C}_{4}\text{H}_{10}$)?
Effusion Time: How long will it take for $50\text{~mL}$ of $\text{O}_{2}$ to effuse through a pinhole if $50\text{~mL}$ of $\text{He}$ takes $12.0\text{~seconds}$ under identical conditions?

Partial Pressure Fraction: A gaseous mixture consists of $60.0$ mole percent $\text{N}_{2}$ and $40.0$ mole percent $\text{O}_{2}$. If the total pressure is $750\text{~mmHg}$, what is the partial pressure of $\text{O}_{2}$?
Kinetic Energy Comparison: Compare $1\text{~mole}$ of $\text{He}$ gas and $1\text{~mole}$ of $\text{Xe}$ gas at the same temperature ($25^{\circ}\text{C}$). Which of the following statements is true?
choices: $\text{He}$ has a higher average kinetic energy than $\text{Xe}$.
$\text{Xe}$ has a higher average kinetic energy than $\text{He}$.
Both gases have the exact same average kinetic energy.
$\text{He}$ molecules travel slower on average than $\text{Xe}$ molecules.

stem:
Hess’s Law. Given the thermochemical equations:

1. $C(graphite) + O_{2}(g) \rightarrow CO_{2}(g)\quad\Delta H^{\circ} = - 393.5\text{~kJ/mol}$

2. $H_{2}(g) + \frac{1}{2}O_{2}(g) \rightarrow H_{2}O(l)\quad\Delta H^{\circ} = - 285.8\text{~kJ/mol}$

3. $2C_{2}H_{2}(g) + 5O_{2}(g) \rightarrow 4CO_{2}(g) + 2H_{2}O(l)\quad\Delta H^{\circ} = - 2598.8\text{~kJ/mol}$

Calculate $\Delta H^{\circ}$ for the formation of acetylene: $2C(graphite) + H_{2}(g) \rightarrow C_{2}H_{2}(g)$.

Enthalpy of Formation: Using standard enthalpies of formation ($\Delta H_{f}^{\circ}$ for $\text{CO}_{2}(g) = - 393.5$, $\text{H}_{2}\text{O}(l) = - 285.8$, $\text{CH}_{4}(g) = - 74.8\text{~kJ/mol}$), calculate $\Delta H_{rxn}^{\circ}$ for the combustion of methane:

$$\text{CH}_{4}(g) + 2\text{O}_{2}(g) \rightarrow \text{CO}_{2}(g) + 2\text{H}_{2}\text{O}(l)$$

Calorimetry: When $50.0\text{~mL}$ of $1.00\text{~M~HCl}$ and $50.0\text{~mL}$ of $1.00\text{~M~NaOH}$ are mixed in a coffee-cup calorimeter, the temperature rises from ${21.5}^{\circ}\text{C}$ to ${28.1}^{\circ}\text{C}$. Assuming the specific heat capacity of the solution is $4.18\text{~J/(g} \cdot^{\circ}\text{C)}$ and the density is $1.00\text{~g/mL}$, calculate the enthalpy of neutralization per mole of $\text{HCl}$.

Bomb Calorimetry: A bomb calorimeter has a heat capacity of $3.50\text{~kJ}/^{\circ}\text{C}$. When a $1.50\text{-g}$ sample of glucose is burned in the calorimeter, the temperature increases by ${4.22}^{\circ}\text{C}$. What is the heat of combustion of glucose in $\text{kJ/g}$?

First Law of Thermodynamics: A system absorbs $250\text{~J}$ of heat from its surroundings and does $450\text{~J}$ of expansion work on the surroundings. What is the change in internal energy ($\Delta U$) of the system?

Expansion Work: Calculate the work done ($in\text{~Joules}$) when $2.0\text{~moles}$ of an ideal gas expands isothermally and reversibly from $5.0\text{~L}$ to $20.0\text{~L}$ at $300\text{~K}$. ($R = 8.314\text{~J/(mol} \cdot \text{K)}$)

Bond Enthalpies: Using average bond enthalpies ($\text{C-H} = 413$, $\text{Cl-Cl} = 242$, $\text{C-Cl} = 328$, $\text{H-Cl} = 431\text{~kJ/mol}$), estimate $\Delta H^{\circ}$ for the chlorination of methane:

$$\text{CH}_{4}(g) + \text{Cl}_{2}(g) \rightarrow \text{CH}_{3}\text{Cl}(g) + \text{HCl}(g)$$

Enthalpy of Solution: The lattice energy of $\text{NaCl}$ is $+ 788\text{~kJ/mol}$ and its enthalpy of solution is $+ 4.0\text{~kJ/mol}$. What is the total hydration enthalpy of $\text{Na}^{+}$ and $\text{Cl}^{-}$ ions?
State vs. Path Functions: Which of the following properties is classified as a path function rather than a state function?

Thermochemical Stoichiometry: Given: $2\text{SO}_{2}(g) + \text{O}_{2}(g) \rightarrow 2\text{SO}_{3}(g)\quad\Delta H^{\circ} = - 198\text{~kJ/mol}$. How much heat is released when $1.00\text{~metric~ton}$ ($1.00 \times 10^{6}\text{~g}$) of $\text{SO}_{2}$ ($64.07\text{~g/mol}$) is converted to $\text{SO}_{3}$?
Standard State Definition: Which of the following substances has a standard enthalpy of formation ($\Delta H_{f}^{\circ}$) equal to zero at $25^{\circ}\text{C}$ and $1\text{~atm}$?

Fuel Value: Glucose ($\text{C}_{6}\text{H}_{12}\text{O}_{6}$, molar mass $180.16\text{~g/mol}$) has a standard enthalpy of combustion of $- 2800\text{~kJ/mol}$. What is its fuel value in $\text{kJ/g}$?

Photoelectric Effect: Light with a wavelength of $400\text{~nm}$ strikes a metal surface. If the work function ($\Phi$) of the metal is $2.40\text{~eV}$ ($1\text{~eV} = 1.602 \times 10^{- 19}\text{~J}$), what is the maximum kinetic energy of the emitted photoelectrons? ($h = 6.626 \times 10^{- 34}\text{~J} \cdot \text{s}$, $c = 3.00 \times 10^{8}\text{~m/s}$)
De Broglie Wavelength: What is the de Broglie wavelength of an electron ($mass = 9.109 \times 10^{- 31}\text{~kg}$) traveling at a speed of $2.00 \times 10^{6}\text{~m/s}$?
